commits.summary: prune_workspaces.py: delete jj workspaces only once nothing in them can be lost
commits.body:
llm-dlc/tools/prune_workspaces.py considers every workspace but the default: those jj lists and the directories of forgotten ones (siblings REPO-* whose .jj/repo points here). It reports by default and deletes only with --delete. A workspace is clear when: no process has its cwd or a file open inside it, and no unfinished loop owns it (a stream workspace NAME-STREAM while llm-dlc/loops/NAME.md's status is neither done nor blocked); every commit of ::WS@ outside ::INTO (the default workspace's @-, or --into) is empty and undescribed; and every file, tracked, untracked or gitignored, is recoverable. That means its exact content is a blob reachable from INTO, or a file anywhere in the default workspace (hashed only on a size match, so its 12 GB verification/.state costs a walk), or it lies in a gitignored build-output directory (target/, build/, ...). It reads file contents, so edits jj never snapshotted count. A .git pointer file jj 0.47 writes is metadata; a .git directory blocks. --archive DIR copies would-be-lost files out and verifies each copy. Deletion re-checks use, forgets a listed workspace, removes the directory and runs git worktree prune. Claude Code transcripts under ~/.claude/projects are left alone.

Verified by test_prune_workspaces.py, 12 cases on throwaway colocated jj repos: merged and deleted; an unmerged commit, an unsnapshotted edit, a unique gitignored .env (and --archive keeping it), a tracked dir named build, a forgotten dir with a unique file, a process inside, a .git directory, and an unfinished loop's workspace all block; a run record copied into the default under another name and ignored target/ are clear. A report-only run here (13 s) finds 3 of 13 clear (the engine-priorities leftovers examples, jbmc, native). The four cleanup-* are kept while cleanup.md waits on jobs. Blocked: the foundations streams' gitignored run records in loop-summaries/ (alignment, heap, observations, summaries), three trace logs only in the foundations directory, and the integration directory's merge files. Nothing was deleted.

So that a later stream's records aren't left behind, llm-dlc/tools/run_records.py collect STREAM DEFAULT copies a workspace's run records into the default workspace: only feature-loop records (not integration reports), a copy replaced only by the record it is a start of (records only grow; one that diverged is left and reported), each written atomically. run-streams.sh calls it at its start (records from an interrupted run), after each of a stream's runs (an interrupted one too), and before the merge, whose commit publishes them. test_runs.py's 5 new tests cover it (they errored before run_records.py existed), and the shell function was run against made-up workspaces: one copy, then nothing on a second call or from the default workspace itself. Run over every workspace directory on disk, it found nothing else missing. test_runs (13), test_streams_status, test_review and test_performance pass. sync.py's comment, llm-dlc/README.md and specification.md say how the records come in.

commits.summary: Stub reachability, step 1: an experiment job that has JBMC's solver decide whether VF-015's proof enters the String.format stub (verification pending)
commits.body:
llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md's step 1. The gap preflight counts a stub as entered when JBMC's symbolic execution alone keeps a step of it. For VF-015's proof (prove Hex#toDigit --assume 'ch == 1632' on commons-codec's old Hex), that counts String.format(String, Object[]) as entered on toDigit's exception path, which the assumption makes infeasible. The new verification/triage/stub-reachability.sh reruns that proof unchanged, with JBMC behind a wrapper that records each command and its time. On the proof's harness and command it then tries two methods. (A) --cover location in place of --unwinding-assertions, reading the goals of DecoderException's constructor, of the stub and of toDigit, and once more with --property on one goal. (B) The proof as given, with a rewritten DecoderException whose String.format call first calls a probe that fails an assertion of its own (throw new AssertionError(), as GapIntrinsics.open). Both also run on a control, the same prove without --assume, where the call is reachable. The job's description gives the outcome each method is expected to have.

Checked inline: the script's syntax, its argv rewriting on made-up commands, and its recording wrapper with echo in place of JBMC. No JBMC was run. The brief's Progress records why the probe is a rewritten caller and not a rewritten goto program: jbmc 6.11 can't write a goto binary for goto-instrument. jbmc --help lists --cover only in --unwinding-assertions' line, so whether --cover is accepted is for the job to show.

Verification pending: job 20261107-233000-stub-reachability-step-1-can-jbmc-s-solv (verification/jobs/). Step 2, choosing the method, waits on its result.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 1: the domain gate refuses a claim's domain the check doesn't make
commits.body:
Before, a claim's object domain had options nothing read: made_by (its kind and its constructors' calls) and classes. A claim made field by field, of invariants, or by a factory ran as whatever constructor domain the check happened to make, and the kernel's Pricing#total was verified under it. Now spec::heap::check_with refuses a domain made field by field or of invariants outright, and equivalence::run, given the claim's domain (Options::object_domain), compares its calls and classes with the constructors its harness layout calls in each version (Layout::made_with, in the claim's words, 'before: shop.Quote(long cents, int quantity)') and the classes they make, once the layout is built and before any helper proof, cache lookup or proof. Each side must name exactly what the other does, or the claim is refused as Unsupported, naming both lists. The label stays the claim's own words: the result states the check's domain, and the claim key covers the label. Docs: lib/README.md (the domain gate), the doc comments of ObjectDomain and heap::check.

The reproducer, tests/heap.rs a_domain_made_otherwise_than_the_check_makes_its_inputs_is_refused_and_never_runs_as_the_constructor_domain, failed before (the field-by-field claim was verified) and passes now, with a factory, a constructor left out, another constructor, a call with no version, and a class added or left out. The gate showed that four heap tests had changed a reused kernel claim's classes but kept its Quote constructors; they now name their own kernels' constructors. foundations.rs's foreign-input test now asserts the gate's refusal under the kernel domain, and the foreign-input refusal without it. The whole lib suite passes inline (448 tests, 0 failed).

commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 7: the equivalence harness catches the checked exceptions either version declares, closing VF-015 (verification pending)
commits.body:
VF-015's triage found that the equivalence harness's call handlers caught only a fixed list of unchecked exceptions (harness::EXCEPTIONS), RuntimeException and Error. A checked exception, such as commons-codec's DecoderException in example 109's Hex.toDigit, left EquivalenceHarness.check uncaught, and no equivalence over a method that throws one could be verified; the old job's step 4 passed only because 'test $? -eq 1' also accepts 'cannot be verified'. Now equivalence::run reads both versions' throws clauses (declared_checked: the checked classes, most specific first, with java.lang.Exception among them; unchecked ones are caught by the list already) into harness::Layout::checked. The harness's handlers for each call, in bytecode and in the statement's Java source, are the listed exceptions then those, under before/ for the previous version's application classes (Layout::exceptions), and the interpreter's replay gives each thrown exception the same category. A checked exception thrown on other inputs, of another class, or by one version alone is a difference; one both throw alike is the same outcome. A method without a throws clause gets exactly the harness it had, so cached proofs of it stay valid. The statement names the declared classes among the exceptions compared. Docs: lib/README.md, regression step 2.

Reproducers: tests/integration.rs a_method_that_declares_a_checked_exception_is_compared_on_it_and_a_change_in_it_is_found failed before (native engine) with 'an uncaught before.fixtures.BadDigit leaves the harness'; now the rewrite is verified and three defects are refuted on the exception, each witness replayed. commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 2: the four interfaces as types in spec/plans.rs, each refused until its stream builds it
commits.body:
The application-core streams meet at four interfaces, now types in lib/src/spec/plans.rs that extend the foundations IR rather than compete with it: a construction plan (ConstructionPlan: a bounded DAG of constructor- or factory-made nodes with stable ids, shared nodes for aliasing, typed leaves, bounded arrays, adapted values, dependencies the environment stands for, the roots, an optional short setup sequence and the domain's restrictions; shape_problem names a cycle, a duplicate, a dangling id, a choice of another class or a bound exceeded), carried by a new Construction::Planned domain; a value domain (ValueDomain, with its model's evidence level, from implemented to proved) and the witness value a replay rebuilds (WitnessValue, UTF-16 code units); a modelled call's CallModel (stable id, argument key, query or choice coupling, permitted results or exceptions, bound), carried by ModeledCall's new optional model; and a helper's Summary (read footprint, alias and null facts, domain, bounds, relation, effects, dependency proofs). Every struct refuses unknown fields and every enum unknown variants. Part gains Objects, Values, Environment and Reuse.

Nothing gets read as absent: a planned domain is refused by the heap check (Part::Objects) and a call's model by the effect check (Part::Environment) until those streams build them, and neither is among the claim key's known fields, so a claim with one is uncacheable. Tests: plans.rs's unit tests (round trips, every interface refusing an unknown field or variant, the plan's shape problems), tests/heap.rs a_domain_made_by_a_construction_plan_is_refused_until_the_objects_stream_builds_it, tests/effects.rs a_modelled_calls_model_is_refused_until_the_environment_stream_builds_it; the spec unit tests and the heap, effects, foundations and summaries suites pass inline. Docs: lib/README.md, and the brief's Progress.

Its results/ files were already swept into the application-core Phase 0 step 2 commit by another session's commit; this commit holds only the VF-015 entry update in verification/findings.md.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 3: each stream's module registered, with its call sites in the shared files
commits.body: So that no stream edits a shared file to begin, each of the four streams of llm-dlc/loops/application-core.md has a module of its own, registered in lib.rs: construction.rs (objects: check_plans for a planned domain, receiver for an ordinary receiver, load for --plan FILE), values.rs (the ValueAdapter trait, adapter for a String or List, is_adapted), environment.rs (check_model for a call's model, declared and load for --environment FILE) and reuse.rs (property_lookup and property_store for prove --cache, summaries for a helper). Each returns Unsupported naming its stream until the stream builds its part. The call sites are in place: the domain gate (spec::heap), the instance-method refusals of equivalence and property, their String and List parameter refusals (which add the values stream's words), the effect check for a call's model, property::run under --cache. The CLI flags --plan (equivalence, prove), --environment (effects, compare, through effects::check_builds and compare::Options::environment) and prove --cache load into the checks' options, and the checks refuse what they don't take yet, never ignore it. StatementSpec carries the environment and the summaries a check used.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 5: the frozen fixtures Q, H and L, with their claims and every case's verdict
commits.body:
The acceptance contract's three fixture families, frozen before any stream forks, in lib/tests/fixtures/application-core/ (its README says what each does and why). Q (package quotes): QuoteService, an ordinary receiver with a fee policy, asks the Rates query for a code's rate (which may throw the checked RateUnavailable), adds the helper fee(lines) that reads the receiver's policy, takes a tenth off a VIP code (Codes.vip), and announces a positive quote on Events; offerQuote uses a nullable Offer DTO; checked hands back the caller's request. Its refactor keeps the external meaning, and its seven defects are a wrong query key, an ignored rate, a missing catch, an event on the wrong branch, a shorter VIP prefix, a helper reading another field, and a copy in place of the caller's object. H: a Throttle whose after-setup defect only a setup call reaches, and one-short, wrong from construction. L: Basket's total, first and clearAll over an immutable list, with a skipped duplicate, the last for the first, a copied first, and an alias-blind clear.

golden/ holds eight canonical claims with planned domains (construction plans with dependencies, a String code of at most 4 units, quantities of at most 4, the environment model of Rates.rate, Offers.find and Events.send, the two throttle domains, the list of at most 3 lines) and expected.json, every build's verdict under every claim and under five plain regression checks (rows O1, V1, V2, R2). Checked on JDK 25.0.5 with the fixture's Conformance.java, which loads each build in its own class loader with the same dependency stubs: after agrees with before on every case of the grids (30,240, 315 and 43), and each defect differs exactly in the methods its expectations name. tests/application_core.rs starts with the claims' round trips and every build compiling; spec::plans now leaves out an array's false nullability, as a node's.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 4: the integration contract, one test per acceptance row a unit run reaches
commits.body:
lib/tests/application_core.rs, which llm-dlc/tools/application-core-integration.sh runs on the streams' merge while they work, now has a test per row of llm-dlc/loops/application-core-acceptance.md that a unit-level run can reach: G0 (the domain gate on the foundations kernel: field by field, invariants, a factory, a constructor left out and an extra class each refused, the kernel's own claim verified), O1 (the throttle's receiver in the regression and property checks), O2 (checked's identity under its claim), O3 (the constructor-only and one-setup-call throttle claims), V1 (Codes.vip), V2 (the basket's list kernels and claims), E1 and E2 (the quote and offer claims, through the new environment::check), R1 (prove --cache twice), R2 (the fee helper on its own) and J3 (a setup call, a modelled outcome and a value bound each change the claim key, or leave it uncacheable by name). Every check runs on the native engine with a jbmc path that doesn't exist, J2's guard.

Each case must reach the verdict the frozen tests/fixtures/application-core/golden/expected.json fixes, or be refused in the words of a stream that owns its row (Unsupported naming that part, or a refused check saying 'the STREAM stream builds it'); anything else fails, a refusal by another stream included. Today G0 reaches its verdicts and every other row stops at its streams' named refusals. The integration check passes on this commit's working copy: the contract (13 tests), the lib unit tests and the foundations, compare and effects contracts, and build.py's, review, run-record and performance suites.

commits.summary: application-core Phase 0 step 6: the statement and the examples' result schema register the streams' new kinds
commits.body:
So that a stream's results stay valid without a schema edit of its own, the statement (lib/src/statement.rs) and the examples' result schema (examples/schema/result.schema.json, edited as text to keep its layout) now name, as variants or optional fields: a value parameter (ParameterKind::Value, the values stream's String or list); the assumptions environment (a modelled dependency's stubs), summary (a helper's summary in place of its body) and setup (the states a setup sequence reaches); the bounds max_value_length, setup_calls and trace_bound; the value models a check ran under, each with its evidence level from implemented to proved (Models::values); and a replay by model, a JVM under the environment model's stubs, never the real dependency. Each is absent or unchosen until a stream fills it, so every existing statement serializes as before.

All 157 recorded example results still validate against the schema, a statement with each new variant validates, and an unknown evidence level is refused. tests/application_core.rs's the_result_schema_registers_the_statements_new_kinds holds the statement's kinds and the schema together. The whole lib suite passes inline (475 tests, 0 failed), and build.py's suite (189). With this, Phase 0 is committed, but for VF-015's job 20261108-024648, which the pipeline hasn't run; the brief's status names what is left: the user's push and launch, and that job.

commits.summary: application-core: VF-015's job after Phase 0 goes back to the user, its harness cause fixed and another guard in the way
commits.body: VF-015's job 20261108-024648 ran at eea1a8a8 (Phase 0 step 7) and failed at step 5 only, as the verification loop's triage records (ponxovxr). The harness fix works: step 5 no longer fails on the uncaught-exception property, and JBMC proves the harness. The tool then refuses the proof because JBMC runs CharEncoding's and Hex's class initializers, in both versions, as possibly throwing a NullPointerException, which the JVM doesn't (its throwing-initializer guard), a cause separate from VF-015's. Step 4 found the change (toDigit(ch='٧'): before 7), but the new version's replay could not run (String.format depends on the default locale) and the outcome still says reproduced, so its stricter check passed on half a replay. Decision 7 leaves no timebox attempt, so the brief's Progress hands both to the user with three ways a further attempt could go (step 5 on the native engine, a solver check of the initializers' throws, a model of the charset constants), and the replay issue for the objects stream's replay plumbing. Status: blocked on the user's push and launch, and the VF-015 decision.
